temples.name: Chennakeshava Temple
temples.summary: DRAFT: Belur’s Chennakeshava temple is the ceremonial heart of the Hoysala stone tradition—an east-facing ekakuta shrine whose lathe-turned pillars and madanika brackets still read as a completed royal dedication. Unique among this set for its urban temple-street setting and the density of signed sculptor work on the outer walls.
temples.history: DRAFT: Foundation in 1117 is conventionally tied to Vishnuvardhana after his victories in the south. Later Hoysala and Vijayanagara additions enlarged the complex; the stellate vimana profile and soapstone narrative friezes remain the core twelfth-century statement. temples.name: Hoysaleswara Temple
temples.summary: DRAFT: Halebidu’s double shrine is the most expansive Hoysala sculptural programme in this collection—a dvikuta Shiva temple whose outer walls carry stacked friezes of animals, riders, and epic scenes. Unique here for the paired Hoysaleswara–Shantaleswara sanctums facing a shared court.
temples.history: DRAFT: Work began in the 1120s at Dwarasamudra, the Hoysala capital. The temple was never given a finished tower in the way Belur’s shrine was completed; invasions and later neglect left the superstructure incomplete. TODO: verify construction end-date.

temples.history: DRAFT: Built by the general Somanatha during Narasimha III’s reign and consecrated in 1258. The temple stands in a walled courtyard with a pillared corridor; much of the original tower profile survives compared with many earlier Hoysala shrines. TODO: verify later repairs.
